evals.name: lightweight-single-agent
evals.prompt: Run a retro on this session. I just had Claude rename 3 variables in a single file, no errors.
evals.expected_output: A lightweight retro with sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.7, and summary table. Should be concise — no metrics table, no scripts invoked.
assertions: Output contains section 3.1 (What Went Well)
Output contains section 3.2 (What Went Wrong) — should note there were no issues or only minor observations
Output contains section 3.7 (Recommendations)
Output contains a summary table with Run type, Subject, and Files changed
Output does NOT contain a per-agent metrics table (single agent, no structured logs)
Output contains a header line with subject and date (# Retro: ...)
Section 3.7 includes a recommendation to consider model downgrade for simple tasks

evals.name: standard-single-agent-with-errors
evals.prompt: Run a retro on the last session. I asked Claude to build a login page and it guessed the API endpoint wrong twice before reading the existing routes. It also used inline validation instead of the project's zod schemas.
evals.expected_output: A standard-depth retro covering spec quality, tool usage, error recovery, and recommendations pointing to specific files.
assertions: Root cause table classifies the endpoint guessing as 'prompt gap' or 'spec gap'
Root cause table classifies the inline validation as 'prompt gap'
Section 3.3 (Specification & Planning) analyzes whether the prompt was specific enough
Recommendations include a specific file path for each fix (e.g., CLAUDE.md, a skill file)
Each recommendation has What, Where, Why, Priority, Type columns
Retro was saved to ~/.claude/retros/ (markdown + JSON)
Output ends with /improve prompt

evals.name: full-orchestration
evals.prompt: Run a retro on the orchestrator pipeline that just completed. The .orchestrator/ directory has all artifacts.
evals.expected_output: A full-depth retro with per-agent metrics table including cost, model selection analysis, plan quality assessment, coordination analysis, trends, and save.
assertions: parse-metrics.py was invoked against .orchestrator/
Per-agent metrics table includes Model and Est. Cost columns
Pipeline total cost is computed at the bottom of the metrics table
Section 3.3 references orchestration-deep-dive.md for plan quality
Section 3.5 references orchestration-deep-dive.md for coordination
Model selection section identifies downgrade candidates with rationale
Subject was extracted from orchestrator artifacts (not guessed)
Trends were checked via retro-history.py with --subject flag
Full retro markdown saved to ~/.claude/retros/
Summary JSON saved with subject, run_type, and project fields
Output does NOT end with /improve prompt (orchestrator handles the gate)

evals.name: edge-case-no-git-repo
evals.prompt: Run a retro on this session. We're not in a git repo — I was just having Claude analyze a PDF and summarize it.
evals.expected_output: A lightweight retro that gracefully skips git commands and relies on conversation history only.
assertions: Retro does not fail due to missing git repo
Data collection notes that git history is unavailable
Analysis is based on conversation context
Retro is still saved to ~/.claude/retros/
